recent_posts.title: Connecting an AWS EKS Argo CD instance to Octopus Cloud
recent_posts.summary: Step-by-step guide to connecting an Argo CD instance running on AWS EKS to Octopus Cloud. Covers provisioning an EKS cluster with eksctl, installing Argo CD via Helm with a dedicated Octopus service account and RBAC policy, generating an authentication token, and using the Octopus connection wizard to install the Octopus Argo gateway via a generated Helm command. Also compares Octopus Cloud vs self-hosted Octopus tradeoffs around networking complexity and data residency requirements.

recent_posts.title: Continuous Delivery Office Hours Ep.4: Mono, micro, mesco
recent_posts.summary: A discussion on choosing between monolithic, microservice, and hybrid ('mescoservice') architectures for software delivery. Key factors include team structure, Conway's Law and the inverse Conway maneuver, deployment model (SaaS vs self-hosted), and data ownership. Common microservice failure modes are covered, such as distributed monoliths and shared databases. The fitness test for any architecture is independent deployability — teams should be able to deploy or commit changes without cross-team coordination.

recent_posts.title: Safely creating projects with the AI Assistant
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough on using the Octopus Deploy AI Assistant Chrome extension to create deployment projects via natural language prompts. The assistant generates OpenTofu code to configure projects deterministically. The post also covers using Git-backed Config as Code as a safety net, allowing teams to audit, inspect, and revert AI-generated changes through standard Git workflows. Tips are included for writing effective prompts and knowing when to manually fine-tune after AI scaffolding.

recent_posts.title: Platforms before portals, build the roads before you buy the GPS
recent_posts.summary: Platform engineering teams often rush to build or buy a developer portal before their underlying platform is ready to support one. Using a GPS-and-roads analogy, the argument is that a portal only amplifies what already exists — if the foundations are inconsistent or fragile, the portal makes those problems more visible, not less. Solid platform foundations (standardization, governance, self-service workflows, reliable pipelines) must come first. Portals do have genuine value, particularly for service discoverability at scale, but most teams aren't ready for them yet. A practical self-check: if you built a portal today and couldn't fill it with working, valuable capabilities, there's more platform work to do first.

recent_posts.title: Continuous Delivery Office Hours Ep.3: Branching strategies
recent_posts.summary: Branching strategy has a direct impact on a team's ability to practice Continuous Delivery. Gitflow is identified as the worst strategy due to its complexity, coordination overhead, and risk of lost bug fixes. Trunk-based development is recommended as the best approach, where all commits go directly to the main branch, complemented by feature toggles, automated checks, and short-lived branches (3 or fewer, under a day old). DORA research supports this, linking trunk-based development and small batch sizes to elite software delivery performance. Team-wide alignment is essential for trunk-based development to succeed.

recent_posts.title: Proactive Dependency Security Best Practices
recent_posts.summary: Supply chain attacks on npm packages like axios highlight the need for proactive dependency security. This guide walks through setting up daily SBOM security scans using Octopus Deploy, leveraging a dedicated Security environment and lifecycle alongside a daily trigger that rescans production dependencies. The pattern ensures vulnerabilities discovered after deployment are caught quickly, complementing CI-time SAST/DAST scanning with continuous production monitoring.

recent_posts.title: Practical Platform Engineering in 5 Lunches: 5. Policies
recent_posts.summary: Part 5 of a series on building an Internal Developer Platform (IDP) with Octopus Deploy, focusing on policies as guardrails for organizational compliance. The tutorial walks through activating a sample policy that requires a manual intervention step in all deployments, intentionally triggering a policy violation by removing that step, observing the resulting deployment failure, and using an AI-powered 'Suggest a fix' feature to resolve the violation. Policies in Platform Hub allow platform teams to enforce standards across projects at scale.

recent_posts.title: Practical Platform Engineering in 5 Lunches: 4. Shared Responsibility of Projects
recent_posts.summary: Part 4 of a 5-part series on building an Internal Developer Platform with Octopus Deploy. Covers structuring deployment projects to support a shared responsibility model, where multiple teams (platform and security) own different stages of the deployment process using process templates arranged in an 'onion' pattern. Explains how pre/post-deploy hook templates allow each team to maintain their portion of the pipeline, and connects this to Conway's Law. Also touches on Git-based workflows and SemVer for managing process templates at scale.

recent_posts.title: Practical Platform Engineering in 5 Lunches: 1. Getting Started
recent_posts.summary: An introductory post in a 5-part series on building an Internal Developer Platform (IDP) using Octopus Deploy. Covers setting up a free Octopus Cloud trial and the Octopus AI Assistant Chrome extension, then defines key terms: DevOps (broadly, any tech team practice), Platform Engineering (scaling architectural decisions), and IDP (tools and processes for distributing those decisions). Explains how Platform Engineering relates to CI/CD and how Octopus Platform Hub supports it through Git-based workflows and SemVer versioning of shared process templates.

recent_posts.title: Verified Argo CD deployments
recent_posts.summary: Octopus Deploy has added a step verification feature to its Argo CD integration, allowing deployments to wait until Argo CD applications are healthy before proceeding. Three verification modes are available: direct commit (existing behavior), pull request merged, and Argo CD application is healthy. A trigger sync option is also introduced to speed up deployments. The post explains how Octopus tracks intended changes using JSON patches and file hashes, and introduces the concept of 'Git drift' to handle scenarios where Argo CD's view diverges from Octopus's committed changes. The feature is available from version 2026.1.

top_posts.title: OWASP Top Ten: 20 years of Application Security
top_posts.summary: Twenty years of OWASP Top 10 data shows application security fundamentals haven't improved—the same vulnerabilities persist across new technologies. SQL injection evolved into NoSQL injection, GraphQL manipulation, and now prompt injection. Broken access control remains the top issue. Supply chain attacks emerged as a major threat vector with npm packages and CI/CD pipelines becoming targets. While authentication improved with passkeys, authorization still fails consistently. The article provides practical guidance: shift-left security with runtime monitoring, assume dependency compromise, treat authorization like authentication, and understand that every developer is part of the security team. Leaders must invest in training, tooling, and observability rather than just buying security products.

top_posts.title: What's new in Argo CD 3.2?
top_posts.summary: Argo CD v3.2 GA release introduces significant improvements across multiple areas: UI enhancements including hydration status on app tiles and sortable columns, ApplicationSet controller performance upgrades with better concurrency and error reporting, new health checks for DatadogMetric resources, server-side diff support for more accurate resource comparison, and Hydrator upgrades with custom commit messages and automatic .gitattributes generation. These changes improve usability, observability, and reliability for teams running GitOps at scale.

top_posts.title: What is GitOps?
top_posts.summary: GitOps is a relatively new addition to the growing list of "Ops" paradigms taking shape in our industry. It all started with DevOps, and while the term DevOps has been around for some years now, it seems we still can't agree whether it's a process, mindset, job title, set of tools.

top_posts.title: Is GitOps right for you?
top_posts.summary: GitOps is a set of principles that enhance continuous delivery (CD) and DevOps practices by using Git as the single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications. While GitOps offers benefits such as better auditability, improved consistency, and increased speed, it also presents challenges like a steep learning curve, secrets management, and managing multiple environments. The post provides insights into setting up pipelines using GitOps and understanding its implications.
